title: Strengths and Limitations of Functionalist, Marxist and Feminist Views of the Role of the Family

titles.subject: Sociology
titles.leaf: Strengths and Limitations of Functionalist, Marxist and Feminist Views of the Role of the Family

author: 68f22f79f52f1eb1cc107ce3
chapter_outcomes: Understand different family structures: nuclear, extended (e.g. modified, horizontal, vertical/beanpole), reconstituted, lone parent, empty nest, childless; strengths and limitations of different family structures
Understand variations and diversity in the family: cross-cultural, social class, ethnicity

Understand sociological views on family diversity: New Right views on family diversity and dysfunctional families, postmodernist views on the positive aspects of family diversity, the extent of family diversity and the dominance of the nuclear family
Understand alternatives to the family: single person households, shared households, friends as family
Understand variations in types of marriage: arranged, empty shell, love, monogamy, serial monogamy

Understand functionalist views: how the family benefits its members and society, functions of the family, the loss of functions debate, how family functions have changed over time, 'warm bath' theory, importance of the nuclear family
Understand Marxist views: how the family benefits capitalism, exploitation of family members, reproduction of class inequalities, family as a unit of consumption, family and ideological control

Understand feminist views: how the family benefits patriarchy and male power, the domestic division of labour, domestic violence and abuse, joint and segregated conjugal roles, dual burden/triple shift, decision-making, gendered socialisation
Understand strengths and limitations of functionalist, Marxist and feminist views of the role of the family
Understand debates about whether the experience of family life is positive or negative for family members
Understand demographic factors and their effects on family life: family size, birth rates, life expectancy, ageing population, having children in later life
Understand the impact of industrialisation and urbanisation on family structures and roles

Understand explanations of changing patterns and trends in marriage, divorce and cohabitation: legislation, societal attitudes and values, role of the internet, secularisation, cultural expectations, changes in the status and power of women/female empowerment
Understand alternatives to marriage: cohabitation, singlehood, lone parents, civil partnerships

Understand changing family roles: changing conjugal roles (more diverse family types, segregated to joint conjugal roles, e.g. symmetrical family, dual worker family, the pivot/sandwich generation); changing roles of children (economic burden/cost, child-centredness, boomerang children); changing roles of grandparents (childcare, economic support, wisdom and advice, dependent/a burden)
